Berothah
be-ROH-thah
proper noun
Hebrew Berothah, “wells” or “cypresses”; a northern border-city, answering to the Berothai from which David took much brass (2Sa 8:8).

📖 Biblical Definition

Berothah is named among the cities of the north border in Ezekiel’s survey of the land: “Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim…” (Eze 47:16), and answers to the Berothai from which David took exceeding much brass for the service of God. In the one place it is a landmark of the kingdom’s far reach; in the other, a spoil of the LORD’s wars adorning His house. Both preach the same thing. The dominion the LORD gave His anointed reached to the distant north, to cities the fathers had never trod, that Jeroboam in his day recovered again for Israel (2Ki 14:28); and the wealth of the vanquished was not squandered but sanctified, carried up to Jerusalem, poured into the vessels of the temple that God might be worshipped. So the far reach of the kingdom and the plunder of its wars alike serve the sanctuary. Herein is a shadow of the greater King, whose dominion shall be from sea to sea, who led captivity captive and received gifts for men, and who spoils the strong man’s house to enrich His own. Every stronghold Christ subdues He turns to the adorning of His church. Berothah, a border-city of brass, tells the saints that no corner of the earth lies beyond their King’s reach, and no spoil of His conquest is lost — all is gathered to the house and glory of God.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A northern border-city (Eze 47:16), answering to the Berothai of David’s spoil; a witness to the far reach of the LORD’s kingdom and the plunder of His wars adorning His house.

BEROTHAH, a city of the north border (Eze 47:16).

Answering to Berothai, whence David took much brass for God’s house.

A landmark of the kingdom’s far northern reach.

The spoil of the LORD’s wars sanctified to the sanctuary.

A figure of the greater King who spoils the strong to enrich His church.

📖 Key Scripture

Eze 47:16 — "Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim, which is between the border of Damascus and the border of Hamath; Hazarhatticon, which is by the coast of Hauran."

2Ki 14:28 — "Now the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, and all that he did, and his might, how he warred, and how he recovered Damascus, and Hamath, which belonged to Judah, for Israel, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?"

1Ch 13:5 — "So David gathered all Israel together, from Shihor of Egypt even unto the entering of Hemath, to bring the ark of God from Kirjathjearim."

Psa 125:2 — "As the mountains are round about Jerusalem, so the LORD is round about his people from henceforth even for ever."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A border-city of brass; it recovers the far reach of the LORD’s kingdom and the spoils of His wars gathered to His house.

expand to see more

A far northern border-city stirs no dispute of the present hour. Its memory serves the sanctuary: the brass of Berothai went up to Jerusalem, and the border of Berothah marked how far the LORD extended the reign of His anointed.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the King’s dominion reaches to the ends of the earth and turns even the spoil of His conquests to the adorning of His church. Christ spoils the strong man’s house; no corner lies beyond His reach, and no plunder of His victory is lost.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The name is bound up with berosh, cypress or fir, and with the sense of wells or springs — a place of trees and waters.

expand to see more

Berothah — Hebrew Berothah, related to wells or cypresses.

Compare berosh, the fir or cypress tree.

Answers to Berothai of 2Sa 8:8, David’s spoil of brass.

Named among the north-border cities (Eze 47:16).

Spelled Berothah in the Authorized Version.

Usage

"Berothah stood on the north border of the land."

"From Berothai David took exceeding much brass."

"Berothah marks the far reach of the kingdom the LORD gave."
